clue.text: Lots of bacteria with wine — that could upset a newcomer

parts.note: bacteria grown in a laboratory dish are cultures, and lots of them are plural
hock is a white wine from the German Rhineland

explanation.surface: A newcomer is put off by a germ-laden glass of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The disorientation felt on arriving in an unfamiliar country or way of life is what knocks a new arrival off balance.

clue.text: Exult over lawyers providing means of exerting leverage

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, that is above, the second

parts.note: to crow is to exult or gloat
the bar is the legal profession of barristers

explanation.surface: Gloating over the lawyers gives someone a hold on them.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron lever with a flattened end is used to prise things open.

clue.text: Miscast roles one plays without success

indicators.note: casting the letters wrongly puts them in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An actor wrongly cast fails in every part played.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who comes off worst in a game or contest is defeated.

clue.text: Star group formed by cub?

parts.note: a young bear is a minor bear, so the constellation named in Latin as the Little Bear fits

explanation.definitionFit: This northern constellation's Latin name means the Lesser Bear, and a cub is a little bear.

clue.text: Sin, as it happens, overthrown

indicators.note: overthrown in a down clue turns the word upside down, so it reads upwards

parts.note: a live broadcast goes out as events happen

explanation.surface: Wrongdoing, at the moment it occurs, is toppled.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness and wrongdoing are synonyms of sin.

clue.text: Republic has changed round internally

indicators.note: internally says the scrambled word goes inside the other word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of round are rearranged

explanation.surface: A republic has altered its course from within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' reads as part of 'changed round', but 'changed' alone is the anagram signal and 'round' is its fodder; 'internally' puts the result inside HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: This Central American country is a republic.

clue.text: Dull report from Conservative seat

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative in British politics
the rump, or buttocks, is what one sits on

explanation.surface: A tedious account from a Tory constituency.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffled thud from an exploding shell is a dull bang.

clue.text: Flowers can be cheerful, if only in' odd selection

parts.note: glad means cheerful or happy

indicators.note: an odd selection picks the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Blooms can brighten things, if only picked at random.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd selection' takes I, O, L, I from IF ONLY IN.
explanation.definitionFit: These sword-leaved garden plants with flower spikes are named in Latin plural.

clue.text: Taking part in dust-up I deemed pointless

indicators.note: the answer takes part in, forming a piece of, the following words

explanation.surface: Someone joins a brawl and judges the whole thing futile.
explanation.definitionFit: Something senseless or futile is foolish.

clue.text: Thing that confuses bosses, having no-one around

indicators.note: confusing the word bosses scrambles its letters into a fresh order
around tells us to turn the no-one piece so it reads backwards

parts.note: no is NO and one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Something baffles the managers because nobody is about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no-one' is split into its parts, NO and ONE, with ONE as the Roman numeral I, before 'around' turns them.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a thing about something is idiom for being fixated on it.

clue.text: Place for Frenchman to sleep in dark

definitions.meaning: French for a bed, '...', read as one word
without light, as a darkened room

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is in French: 'un lit' means a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A room with no lamp switched on is dark, and in French a bed is un lit.

clue.text: British engineers going over one old warship

indicators.note: the engineers' letters go over, that is around, the numeral, enclosing it

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: British army engineers clamber over an ancient warship.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley of ancient times with two banks of oars was a fighting ship.

clue.text: Upstart cleared fence on horse .

parts.note: a horse that clears a fence has jumped it
a rider on horseback is said to be up

explanation.surface: A show jumper clears a fence, and the upstart rider is cocky.
explanation.walkthrough: In racing a jockey is 'up' when mounted on the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has risen above their station and behaves arrogantly is a parvenu or upstart.

clue.text: Advancing insurrection

definitions.meaning: a revolt or uprising against authority

explanation.definitionFit: Prices going up are advancing, and a popular revolt is an uprising.

clue.text: Agonised when lost in US city

indicators.note: letters that are lost wander out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone suffered anguish on getting lost in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: A Californian city on the Pacific coast near Mexico.

clue.text: Old man's weapon that's needed to gain access

parts.note: the old man is father, or pa, so his is pa's
a sword is a bladed weapon

explanation.surface: Dad's sword is the key to getting in.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret word spoken or typed is what a guard or computer demands before letting you through.

clue.text: Opera producer arranged trial with cast

indicators.note: arranging the words puts their letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre producer set up a trial with the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opera producer' suggests a stage impresario; it is a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alessandro Scarlatti was an Italian Baroque composer who wrote many operas.

clue.text: Heavily built and unintelligent pupils

parts.note: thick is slang for stupid
a set is a group of pupils taught together

explanation.surface: Burly and dim schoolchildren.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocky or burly describes someone with a solid, heavy frame.

clue.text: State of butterfly unknown

parts.note: the monarch is a large orange butterfly
Y is an algebraic unknown, as in x and y

explanation.surface: Describing the condition of a mysterious butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: A country ruled by a king or queen is one kind of nation.

clue.text: Spanish port wine

definitions.meaning: a port city on the Costa del Sol
a sweet fortified wine from that region

explanation.definitionFit: Malaga is an Andalusian seaport and gives its name to a sweet dessert wine.

clue.text: Saw article's extremely high values

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or maxim
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An article on carpentry tools turns out to be very valuable.
explanation.definitionFit: The greatest values a quantity reaches are its peaks, in Latin plural form.

clue.text: He served Caesar, J. — all for nothing, perhaps

definitions.meaning: written surname first like 'Caesar, J.', Mark Antony who served Julius Caesar is '....'
nothing is the opposite of all

explanation.walkthrough: 'Caesar, J.' is Julius Caesar listed surname first; his follower Mark Antony listed the same way is ANTONY, M.
explanation.definitionFit: A word of opposite meaning, as nothing is to all, is the reverse of a synonym.

clue.text: Dial not affected by stress

parts.note: the word dial read back to front spells laid, so laid read back gives dial

explanation.surface: Turning a dial with no pressure involved.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: LAID with BACK as an instruction makes DIAL, the clue word.
explanation.definitionFit: A relaxed, easy-going person is untroubled by pressure.

clue.text: Sword finishes off William and Robert quickly

indicators.note: finishes off says the last letter of each name is cut away

parts.note: Bill is a pet form of William
Bob is a pet form of Robert

explanation.surface: A blade quickly does for Bill and Bob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishes off' removes the last letter of BILL and of BOB; 'quickly' only colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A bilbo is an old Spanish sword named after Bilbao.

clue.text: Nearly a couple of pounds to save

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra, so two of them make LL
save means except, as does but in 'everyone but me'

explanation.surface: Almost two pounds to put by.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost or practically is the meaning of this phrase, as in 'virtually finished'.

clue.text: Animated bounder in 'computer company Jack set up

indicators.note: set up in a down clue turns the pieces so they read upwards

parts.note: IBM is the American computer company
a jack is a sailor, an AB or able seaman

explanation.surface: A cartoon cad works in a computer firm that a sailor founded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns IBM + AB into BAMBI.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney's cartoon fawn bounds about the forest, so a leaping deer on film.

clue.text: As far as possible, find location of heart

definitions.meaning: as in driving a nail fully in
where the heart is, the saying goes

explanation.definitionFit: Driving a nail home pushes it fully in, and the proverb places the heart at one's house.

clue.text: Author adding line to essay repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly says the attempt word is given twice in a row

parts.note: an essay is an attempt, or a go

explanation.surface: A writer keeps adding a line to an essay.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikolai Gogol was the Russian writer of Dead Souls and The Overcoat.

clue.text: Bishop, for example, initially wears blue

indicators.note: initially here says the word for wears comes at the start, ahead of the chess piece

parts.note: to sport something is to wear it
a bishop is one of the chessmen, a man on the board

explanation.surface: A clergyman puts on blue vestments at first.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge a 'blue' is someone who has represented the university at sport.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxbridge blue is an athlete awarded colours for university sport.

clue.text: PM promised time for reform

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters of the two words are rebuilt

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister pledged a moment for reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' looks like the Prime Minister but is the Latin afternoon abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation stands for the Latin phrase meaning after midday.
